column1: What does a scalar user-defined function return?
column2:
One value of a declared SQL data type.
It returns a scalar value rather than a table.
Review source

column1: What is the minimum number of input parameters for a scalar UDF?
column2:
Zero.
A function without parameters still requires parentheses in its declaration and calls.
Review source

column1: What distinguishes scalar UDF usage from an ordinary stored-procedure call?
column2:
A scalar UDF can be used inside a SQL expression.
Fabric Warehouse scalar UDFs are in preview and must qualify for inlining in SELECT...FROM queries on user tables.
Review source | Fabric Warehouse

column1: Which clause declares a scalar UDF's return data type?
column2:
RETURNS.
For example, RETURNS DECIMAL(10,2) declares the tax function's result type.
Review source

column1: How does RETURN in a scalar UDF differ from RETURN in a stored procedure?
column2:
The UDF returns its calculated value, not an integer execution-status code.
The function's RETURNS clause defines the result type.
Review source

column1: Why put a shared calculation in a scalar UDF?
column2:
To keep one reusable implementation of the calculation.
A rule change can be made in the function rather than repeated across queries.
Review source

column1: What makes a function deterministic?
column2:
It returns the same result for the same inputs and database state.
Reading the changing system clock can break this property.
Review source

column1: Why does GETDATE() make the unit's tenure UDF unsuitable for use in an indexed view?
column2:
GETDATE() makes the function nondeterministic.
An indexed view cannot reference a nondeterministic function.
Review source

column1: Which redesign removes the clock dependency from a date-dependent UDF?
column2:
Accept an explicit as-of date instead of calling GETDATE().
Deterministic logic also needs schema binding to be marked deterministic by SQL Server.
Review source

column1: Which restriction prevents a T-SQL scalar UDF from directly updating application tables?
column2:
UDFs cannot directly modify permanent database state.
Use a stored procedure when the operation must change application data.
Review source

column1: Why must callers not rely on the exact number or order of scalar UDF evaluations?
column2:
Query optimization can change how the function is evaluated.
Keep the function free of side effects rather than relying on evaluation timing.
Review source

column1: Why can a non-inlined scalar UDF be costly on a large result set?
column2:
Repeated function calls can add overhead for every qualifying row.
Statement-by-statement function execution also limits optimization across its statements.
Review source

column1: Which SQL Server 2019-and-later feature can remove separate calls to eligible T-SQL scalar UDFs?
column2:
Scalar UDF inlining.
The optimizer substitutes expressions or subqueries, but not every function or call qualifies.
Review source

column1: Which function form exposes reusable tabular query logic as a single SELECT statement?
column2:
An inline table-valued function.
It returns a table, so replacing a scalar UDF requires rewriting the calling query.
Review source

column1: Why does DATEDIFF(YEAR, @HireDate, @AsOfDate) not always give completed tenure years?
column2:
It counts year boundaries, not completed anniversaries.
The unit's simple tenure expression can overstate completed years before the hire-date anniversary.
Review source

column1: Why cannot a VARCHAR(10) function parameter reliably preserve phone input longer than ten ASCII characters?
column2:
The value can be truncated before the function body sees it.
An internal length check cannot inspect characters already lost during parameter conversion.
Review source

column1: Which statement changes an existing scalar UDF without dropping its permissions?
column2:
ALTER FUNCTION.
Review callers if its parameters or return type change.
Review source

column1: What error does DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS avoid?
column2:
The missing-function error when the named function does not exist.
It does not bypass permission checks or dependency restrictions.
Review source

column1: Which catalog view helps inspect recorded SQL dependencies before dropping a function?
column2:
sys.sql_expression_dependencies.
Review references to the function before removing it.
Review source

column1: What kind of function or view dependency can block DROP FUNCTION?
column2:
A schema-bound function or view that references the function.
IF EXISTS does not override this dependency restriction.
Review source

column1: What naming form is required when invoking a scalar UDF in a SELECT expression?
column2:
At least schema.function_name, such as dbo.CalculateSalesTax.
The schema-qualified function name is followed by parentheses containing its arguments.
Review source
